<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead" summary="Fix nil-price invoice crash">
Fix accepted HIGH issue ec8e6c8d-fb54-48bb-be1c-caf0d5a6e54e in /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm: completing a job whose agreed_price_cents is nil crashes invoice generation with a Postgrex NOT NULL violation (invoices.amount_cents). Reachable in real usage: CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1 materializes recurring-plan visits WITHOUT a price, so completing any plan-generated job crashes.

You own lib/cleaner_crm/billing*, lib/cleaner_crm/scheduling/recurrence.ex, and lib/cleaner_crm/scheduling.ex (plan/price plumbing only). MCP note: on "No session_id available" add session_id "b82dc084-1093-4624-b490-31c68a31a4a8"; if MCP hangs >2 min, message me and keep coding.

Fix BOTH ends: (1) recurring plans should carry a price to their visits — check whether Plan has an agreed_price/rate field; if yes, Recurrence.job_attrs copies it; if no, add agreed_price_cents to Plan (migration + plan form field in schedule_live/plan form if trivial — if the form edit risks conflicts, skip the UI and note it) and copy it to materialized jobs, nil allowed. (2) Billing's invoice-on-completion must handle nil price GRACEFULLY: skip invoice creation, and make it visible instead of silent (e.g. {:error, :no_price} handled by the caller — job still completes, office sees the invoice missing; document in the function; if InvoiceLive lists jobs-without-invoices naturally that's enough). Job completion must NEVER crash on nil price.

Verify: MIX_ENV=test mix compile clean; regression test for both paths (complete nil-price job → completes, no invoice, no crash; plan visit carries plan price); FULL PORT=4002 MIX_ENV=test mix test (163+ / 0, includes Wallaby journeys — do NOT break them); mix spex 836_*/ 833_*/ 846_*/ green; mix format. NO dev compile/server restart — say "NEEDS RELEASE REBUILD". resolve_issue when green. Final response: files, decisions made, counts. Under 150 words.

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence do
  @moduledoc """
  Generates the dates for a plan's series from its cadence.

  Project-local, calendar-date arithmetic (see the recurrence ADR) —
  no RRULE library, no virtual occurrences. `:weekly` steps 7 days,
  `:biweekly` 14, `:monthly` 28 (a fixed 4-week cadence, not a calendar
  month, so the weekday never drifts).

  TODO: the recurrence ADR calls for materializing against each
  account's IANA timezone (via `tzdata`) so visits stay pinned to local
  wall-clock across DST, plus a rolling 12-week horizon extended by a
  daily Oban job. Neither is implemented yet — dates here are naive
  and every plan is materialized in full up front, bounded only by its
  own `occurrence_count`.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan

  @step_days %{weekly: 7, biweekly: 14, monthly: 28}

  @doc """
  Returns a list of `%{index:, date:}` maps, one per occurrence, in
  series order starting at 1. `nil` if the plan is missing any of the
  fields a series needs.
  """
  def occurrences(%RecurringPlan{
        recurrence: recurrence,
        start_date: %Date{} = start_date,
        occurrence_count: count
      })
      when recurrence in [:weekly, :biweekly, :monthly] and is_integer(count) and count > 0 do
    step = Map.fetch!(@step_days, recurrence)

    for index <- 1..count do
      %{index: index, date: Date.add(start_date, (index - 1) * step)}
    end
  end

  def occurrences(_incomplete_plan), do: []

  @doc """
  Job attribute maps ready for `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job/2`, one
  per occurrence.
  """
  def job_attrs(%RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    Enum.map(occurrences(plan), fn %{date: date} ->
      %{
        property_id: plan.property_id,
        cleaner_id: plan.cleaner_id,
        recurring_plan_id: plan.id,
        scheduled_date: date,
        start_time: plan.start_time,
        end_time: plan.end_time
      }
    end)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan do
  @moduledoc """
  A weekly/biweekly/monthly cadence for a property that materializes a
  series of `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job` rows (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`).

  `cleaner_id` is the client's *preferred* cleaner (story 846): every
  job generated from this plan defaults to this cleaner, and
  reassigning a single visit away from them is a warning, not a block.
  It is optional — a plan with no preferred cleaner generates
  unassigned jobs and never warns on reassignment.

  `start_time`/`end_time` default to a plain 9am-11am visit window;
  nothing in the plan form asks for these explicitly today, but every
  generated job needs a concrete time to run conflict detection
  against.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurrence: :weekly | :biweekly | :monthly | nil,
          start_date: Date.t() | nil,
          occurrence_count: integer() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "recurring_plans" do
    field :recurrence, Ecto.Enum, values: [:weekly, :biweekly, :monthly]
    field :start_date, :date
    field :occurrence_count, :integer
    field :start_time, :time, default: ~T[09:00:00]
    field :end_time, :time, default: ~T[11:00:00]

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(property_id cleaner_id recurrence start_date occurrence_count start_time end_time)a

  @doc """
  Changeset for the fully-specified plan a save requires.
  """
  def changeset(plan, attrs) do
    plan
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:property_id, :recurrence, :start_date, :occurrence_count])
    |> validate_number(:occurrence_count, greater_than: 0)
  end

  @doc """
  Changeset for the live preview as the owner fills in the form —
  every field is optional so the conflict list can update incrementally
  as soon as enough of them are present, well before the plan is valid
  enough to save.
  """
  def preview_changeset(plan, attrs) do
    cast(plan, attrs, @fields)
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Invoices generated from completed jobs and payment collection via
4	  card-on-file or a public payment link, with proof-of-work attached
5	  from `CleanerCrm.Quality` for chargeback defense.
6	
7	  Per the payments-stripe ADR, an invoice's `status` only ever advances
8	  on a Stripe webhook confirmation: `charge_card/2` and
9	  `pay_via_link/2` just submit a PaymentIntent and move the invoice to
10	  `:charge_pending`; only `receive_webhook/1` marks it `:paid`, or
11	  reverts it to `:unpaid` on a decline so the owner can retry or send a
12	  payment link.
13	
14	  Every function that isn't reached from the public `/pay/:token` or
15	  `/webhooks/stripe` routes is scoped to the caller's active account —
16	  those two have no logged-in user to scope against.
17	
18	  ## Job completion integration point
19	
20	  No caller generates an invoice automatically yet: job completion
21	  itself lives in `CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_job/2`
22	  (`CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job`, which will drive it, doesn't exist
23	  yet either). Once it does, the natural hook is right there — call
24	  `generate_for_job/2` with the now-completed job after
25	  `Quality.complete_job/2` succeeds.
26	  """
27	
28	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
29	
30	  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.{Invoice, Payment, ReceiptNotifier, StripeGateway}
31	  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
32	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
33	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
34	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
35	
36	  ## Invoices

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing do
  @moduledoc """
  Invoices generated from completed jobs and payment collection via
  card-on-file or a public payment link, with proof-of-work attached
  from `CleanerCrm.Quality` for chargeback defense.

  Per the payments-stripe ADR, an invoice's `status` only ever advances
  on a Stripe webhook confirmation: `charge_card/2` and
  `pay_via_link/2` just submit a PaymentIntent and move the invoice to
  `:charge_pending`; only `receive_webhook/1` marks it `:paid`, or
  reverts it to `:unpaid` on a decline so the owner can retry or send a
  payment link.

  Every function that isn't reached from the public `/pay/:token` or
  `/webhooks/stripe` routes is scoped to the caller's active account —
  those two have no logged-in user to scope against.

  ## Job completion integration point

  No caller generates an invoice automatically yet: job completion
  itself lives in `CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_job/2`
  (`CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job`, which will drive it, doesn't exist
  yet either). Once it does, the natural hook is right there — call
  `generate_for_job/2` with the now-completed job after
  `Quality.complete_job/2` succeeds.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.{Invoice, Payment, ReceiptNotifier, StripeGateway}
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  ## Invoices

  @doc "Lists the account's invoices, most recent first, for the billing queue."
  def list_invoices(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([i], desc: i.inserted_at)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_invoice!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  @doc """
  Looks up an invoice by its public payment-link token. Takes no
  `Scope` — the payer on `/pay/:token` isn't a logged-in user, so the
  token itself (unguessable, unique) is the only access control this
  lookup has.
  """
  def get_invoice_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.payment_token == ^token)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def create_invoice(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Invoice{account_id: account_id}
    |> Invoice.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Generates the invoice for a job that's just been marked complete —
  see the moduledoc for where this gets wired in once job completion
  has a real caller.
  """
  def generate_for_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, amount_cents: job.agreed_price_cents, status: :unpaid})
  end

  ## Payment collection

  @doc """
  Charges the client's card on file for the invoice's full amount.
  Refused with `{:error, :no_card_on_file}` when the client has none.
  """
  def charge_card(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> invoice_client()
    |> submit_and_finalize_charge(invoice, off_session: true, source: "card_on_file")
  end

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{card_on_file: false}, _invoice, _opts),
    do: {:error, :no_card_on_file}

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{} = client, invoice, opts) do
    {source, charge_opts} = Keyword.pop!(opts, :source)

    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           submit_charge(invoice, payment_method_for(client), charge_opts) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, client, intent_id, source)
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Charges the given payment method against the invoice reached via its
  public payment-link token — the `/pay/:token` page's own flow, with
  no card on file and no logged-in payer to scope against.
  """
  def pay_via_link(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <- submit_charge(invoice, payment_method, off_session: false) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, invoice_client(invoice), intent_id, "payment_link")
    end
  end

  defp submit_charge(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method, opts) do
    StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      payment_method: payment_method,
      off_session: Keyword.get(opts, :off_session, false),
      metadata: %{invoice_id: invoice.id}
    })
  end

  # Clients doesn't yet persist a real Stripe payment-method/customer id
  # (only the `card_on_file` flag) — this placeholder stands in until a
  # SetupIntent-backed token is stored. The Test adapter ignores it
  # entirely, and the Live adapter is never exercised without one.
  defp payment_method_for(%Client{id: id}), do: "card_on_file:#{id}"

  defp finalize_charge_submission(%Invoice{} = invoice, client, intent_id, source) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <-
             invoice
             |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: :charge_pending, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id})
             |> Repo.update(),
           {:ok, _payment} <- record_payment(updated, intent_id, source, :pending) do
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
    |> tap(fn
      {:ok, updated} -> send_receipt(client, updated)
      _error -> :ok
    end)
  end

  @doc """
  Generates (or reuses) an invoice's public payment-link token, so the
  owner can share `/pay/:token` with a client who has no card on file.
  """
  def create_payment_link(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> Invoice.changeset(%{payment_token: invoice.payment_token || generate_token()})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)

  defp invoice_client(%Invoice{} = invoice) do
    invoice |> Repo.preload(job: :client) |> then(& &1.job.client)
  end

  defp send_receipt(%Client{email: email}, %Invoice{} = invoice) when is_binary(email) do
    ReceiptNotifier.deliver_receipt(email, invoice)
    :ok
  end

  defp send_receipt(_client, _invoice), do: :ok

  defp record_payment(%Invoice{} = invoice, intent_id, source, status) do
    %Payment{account_id: invoice.account_id, invoice_id: invoice.id}
    |> Payment.changeset(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      status: status,
      provider: "stripe",
      stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id,
      source: source
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Webhook

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request — the
  controller's only touchpoint into this context, so it never sees
  event data it can't trust.
  """
  def receive_webhook(conn) do
    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
      apply_webhook_event(event)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :paid, :succeeded)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :unpaid, :failed)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:ok, :ignored}

  defp find_invoice_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => invoice_id}} when is_binary(invoice_id) ->
        fetch_invoice(invoice_id)

      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) ->
        fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id)

      _ ->
        {:error, :invoice_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice(invoice_id) do
    case Repo.get(Invoice, invoice_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Invoice, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  # `stripe_payment_intent_id` is left as-is on a decline (never
  # cleared) — its presence is what tells `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show`
  # to offer "retry" instead of the initial "charge card" action.
  defp transition_invoice(%Invoice{} = invoice, new_status, payment_status) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <- invoice |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: new_status}) |> Repo.update() do
        update_payment_record(updated, payment_status)
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
  end

  # The `Payment` submitted alongside the charge is normally still
  # `:pending` here and just gets its outcome filled in; a fixture-seeded
  # invoice (no prior `charge_card/2` call) has none, so one is created
  # for the audit trail.
  defp update_payment_record(%Invoice{} = invoice, status) do
    case Repo.get_by(Payment,
           invoice_id: invoice.id,
           stripe_payment_intent_id: invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id
         ) do
      nil -> record_payment(invoice, invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id, "webhook", status)
      payment -> payment |> Payment.changeset(%{status: status}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end
end

10	  """

13	  import Ecto.Changeset
14	
15	  @type status :: :unpaid | :charge_pending | :paid
16	
17	  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
18	          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
19	          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
20	          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
21	          amount_cents: integer() | nil,
22	          status: status(),

24	          payment_token: String.t() | nil,
25	          job: CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job.t() | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
26	          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
27	          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
28	        }
29	
30	  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
31	  schema "invoices" do
32	    field :amount_cents, :integer
33	    field :amount, :decimal, virtual: true
34	    field :status, Ecto.Enum, values: [:unpaid, :charge_pending, :paid], default: :unpaid
35	    field :stripe_payment_intent_id, :string
36	    field :payment_token, :string
37	
38	    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
39	    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id
40	
41	    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
42	  end
43	
44	  @fields ~w(job_id amount amount_cents status stripe_payment_intent_id payment_token)a
45	
46	  def changeset(invoice, attrs) do
47	    invoice
48	    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
49	    |> validate_required([:job_id])
50	    |> put_amount_cents()
51	    |> validate_number(:amount_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
52	    |> unique_constraint(:payment_token)
53	  end
54	
55	  # `amount` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the money-handling
56	  # ADR); rounded half-up and stored as `amount_cents` — the only column

58	  # `agreed_price_cents`) pass `amount_cents` directly and skip this.
59	  defp put_amount_cents(changeset) do
60	    case get_change(changeset, :amount) do
61	      nil ->
62	        changeset
63	
64	      %Decimal{} = amount ->
65	        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
66	        put_change(changeset, :amount_cents, cents)
67	    end
68	  end

    field :status, Ecto.Enum, values: [:unpaid, :charge_pending, :paid], default: :unpaid
    field :stripe_payment_intent_id, :string
    field :payment_token, :string

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(job_id amount amount_cents status stripe_payment_intent_id payment_token)a

  def changeset(invoice, attrs) do
    invoice
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:job_id])
    |> put_amount_cents()
    |> validate_number(:amount_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> unique_constraint(:payment_token)
  end

  # `amount` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the money-handling
  # ADR); rounded half-up and stored as `amount_cents` — the only column
  # ever persisted. Callers that already have cents (e.g. copying a job's
  # `agreed_price_cents`) pass `amount_cents` directly and skip this.
  defp put_amount_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :amount) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :amount_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).

  ## Pay fields

  `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` describe what the
  *cleaner* earns for this job — as distinct from `agreed_price_cents`,
  what the *client* is charged. They live here rather than on a
  separate table for the same reason `agreed_price_cents` does: a
  job's pay arrangement is a one-off property of that job, read and
  written by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` rather than by Scheduling
  itself.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    field :pay_type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :piece_rate_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price
             pay_type hourly_rate_cents piece_rate_cents)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while some spex drive the same form with a
  # `scheduled_date` override instead (matching the schema field name
  # directly). The form carries a second, always-blank
  # `job[scheduled_date]` field purely as a landing pad for that
  # override key (`Phoenix.LiveViewTest.form/3` requires an override's
  # key to match a real field name in the form). Whichever one arrives
  # non-blank wins; `scheduled_date` takes precedence when both do,
  # since a still-blank landing pad means only `date` was ever touched.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"scheduled_date" => sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, "date")

  defp rename_date_key(%{scheduled_date: sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, :date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

Skipping asks for a reason inline (its own 12 `
`, scoped to that item) rather than hardcoding one; the 13 reason is persisted on the `ChecklistItem` for `QualityLive.Review` 14 to show the owner. 15 16 Each item renders as its own `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistItemComponent` 17 so its before/after photo uploads stay independently scoped. 18 Completing the job also generates its invoice, when 19 `CleanerCrm.Billing` is present — read defensively per the 20 moduledoc note on `CleanerCrm.Billing.generate_for_job/2` about that 21 hook not existing yet everywhere it's called from. 22 23 ## Assigns 24 25 | Assign | Type | Required | Description | 26 |---------------|-------------------|----------|----------------------------------| 27 | id | string | yes | LiveComponent DOM id | 28 | current_scope | `Scope.t()` | yes | caller scope | 29 | job | `Job.t()` | yes | the checklist's job (for billing) | 30 | checklist | `Checklist.t()` | yes | the job's checklist, items preloaded | 31 32 Notifies the parent LiveView with `send(self(), :job_completed)` 33 once the job is marked complete, so it can reload the job and 34 checklist. 35 36 ## Dependencies 37 38 - `CleanerCrm.Quality` 39 - `CleanerCrm.Billing` 40 """ 41 42 use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component 43 44 alias CleanerCrm.Billing 45 alias CleanerCrm.Quality 46 alias CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistItemComponent 47 48 @impl true 49 def render(assigns) do 50 ~H""" 51
52
53
54

Checklist

55 {elem(@progress, 0)} of {elem(@progress, 1)} 56
57 58
63

{room}

64
    65 <.live_component 66 :for={item <- items} 67 module={ChecklistItemComponent} 68 id={"checklist-item-#{item.id}"} 69 current_scope={@current_scope} 70 item={item} 71 /> 72
73
74 75
80
81

Still needed before this job is done:

82
    83
  • 84
    85 {item.task} 86 96
    97 98 106 107 115 122 131
    • 132 133
134
135
136 137 <.button 138 :if={is_nil(@checklist.completed_at)} 139 data-test="mark-complete-button" 140 phx-click="mark_complete" 141 phx-target={@myself} 142 class="mt-3" 143 > 144 Finish Job 145 146
147
148 """ 149 end 150 151 @impl true 152 def update(assigns, socket) do 153 {:ok, 154 socket 155 |> assign(assigns) 156 |> assign(:rooms, Quality.group_by_room(assigns.checklist)) 157 |> assign(:progress, Quality.progress(assigns.checklist)) 158 |> assign(:incomplete, Quality.incomplete_required_items(assigns.checklist)) 159 |> assign_new(:skip_form_item_id, fn -> nil end)} 160 end 161 162 @impl true 163 def handle_event("mark_complete", _params, socket) do 164 scope = socket.assigns.current_scope 165 166 case Quality.complete_job(scope, socket.assigns.checklist) do 167 {:ok, _completed} -> 168 maybe_generate_invoice(scope, socket.assigns.job) 169 send(self(), :job_completed) 170 {:noreply, assign(socket, :incomplete, [])} 171 172 {:error, {:incomplete_required_tasks, incomplete}} -> 173 {:noreply, assign(socket, :incomplete, incomplete)} 174 end 175 end 176 177 def handle_event("show_skip_form", %{"item-id" => item_id}, socket) do 178 {:noreply, assign(socket, :skip_form_item_id, item_id)} 179 end 180 181 def handle_event("cancel_skip_form", _params, socket) do 182 {:noreply, assign(socket, :skip_form_item_id, nil)} 183 end 184 185 def handle_event("skip", %{"item-id" => item_id, "reason" => reason}, socket) do 186 item = Enum.find(socket.assigns.checklist.items, &(&1.id == item_id)) 187 188 case Quality.skip_checklist_item(socket.assigns.current_scope, item, reason) do 189 {:ok, _item} -> 190 send(self(), :checklist_changed) 191 {:noreply, assign(socket, :skip_form_item_id, nil)} 192 193 {:error, _changeset} -> 194 {:noreply, socket} 195 end 196 end 197 198 # Not every account has `CleanerCrm.Billing` wired to this hook yet 199 # (see its moduledoc) — read defensively so this component never 200 # needs to change again once it lands. 201 defp maybe_generate_invoice(scope, job) do 202 if Code.ensure_loaded?(Billing) and function_exported?(Billing, :generate_for_job, 2) do 203 Billing.generate_for_job(scope, job) 204 end 205 end 206 end 207

It carries no params of its own, so it saves whatever the 150 # last "validate" pass put in the form. 151 def handle_event("save", %{"plan" => params}, socket), do: save_plan(socket, params) 152 153 def handle_event("save", _params, socket), 154 do: save_plan(socket, socket.assigns.form.params || %{}) 155 156 defp save_plan(socket, params) do 157 case Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do 158 {:ok, {plan, _jobs}} -> 159 notify_parent({:saved, plan}) 160 changeset = Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.current_scope, plan, %{}) 161 162 {:noreply, 163 socket 164 |> assign(:plan, plan) 165 |> assign_form_and_conflicts(changeset)} 166 167 {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> 168 {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :plan))} 169 end 170 end 171 172 defp assign_form_and_conflicts(socket, changeset) do 173 draft = Ecto.Changeset.apply_changes(changeset) 174 175 conflicts = 176 socket.assigns.current_scope 177 |> Scheduling.preview_conflicts(draft) 178 |> Enum.reject(&MapSet.member?(socket.assigns.overridden, &1.index)) 179 180 socket 181 |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset, as: :plan)) 182 |> assign(:conflicts, conflicts) 183 end 184 185 defp notify_parent(msg), do: send(self(), {__MODULE__, msg}) 186 187 defp list_properties(%{active_account_id: account_id}) do 188 Property 189 |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id) 190 |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address) 191 |> Repo.all() 192 end 193 194 defp property_options(properties), do: Enum.map(properties, &{&1.service_address, &1.id}) 195 defp cleaner_options(cleaners), do: Enum.map(cleaners, &{&1.name || &1.email, &1.id}) 196 197 defp conflict_reason_text(:unavailable), do: "the cleaner is unavailable that day" 198 defp conflict_reason_text(:overlap), do: "it overlaps another booking" 199 200 defp form_title(:new), do: "New Recurring Plan" 201 defp form_title(:edit), do: "Edit Recurring Plan" 202 end 203

It carries no params of its own, so it saves whatever the # last "validate" pass put in the form. def handle_event("save", %{"plan" => params}, socket), do: save_plan(socket, params) def handle_event("save", _params, socket), do: save_plan(socket, socket.assigns.form.params || %{}) defp save_plan(socket, params) do case Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do {:ok, {plan, _jobs}} -> notify_parent({:saved, plan}) changeset = Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.current_scope, plan, %{}) {:noreply, socket |> assign(:plan, plan) |> assign_form_and_conflicts(changeset)} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :plan))} end end defp assign_form_and_conflicts(socket, changeset) do draft = Ecto.Changeset.apply_changes(changeset) conflicts = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Scheduling.preview_conflicts(draft) |> Enum.reject(&MapSet.member?(socket.assigns.overridden, &1.index)) socket |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset, as: :plan)) |> assign(:conflicts, conflicts) end defp notify_parent(msg), do: send(self(), {__MODULE__, msg}) defp list_properties(%{active_account_id: account_id}) do Property |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id) |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address) |> Repo.all() end defp property_options(properties), do: Enum.map(properties, &{&1.service_address, &1.id}) defp cleaner_options(cleaners), do: Enum.map(cleaners, &{&1.name || &1.email, &1.id}) defp conflict_reason_text(:unavailable), do: "the cleaner is unavailable that day" defp conflict_reason_text(:overlap), do: "it overlaps another booking" defp form_title(:new), do: "New Recurring Plan" defp form_title(:edit), do: "Edit Recurring Plan" end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanLive do
  @moduledoc """
  Routes for creating (`:new`) or editing (`:edit`) a recurring plan.
  Hosts `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent`.
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan
  alias CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent

  @impl true
  def render(assigns) do
    ~H"""
    <Layouts.app flash={@flash} current_scope={@current_scope}>
      <.live_component
        module={PlanFormComponent}
        id="plan-form"
        current_scope={@current_scope}
        action={@live_action}
        plan={@plan}
      />
    </Layouts.app>
    """
  end

  @impl true
  def mount(params, _session, socket) do
    {:ok, apply_action(socket, socket.assigns.live_action, params)}
  end

  defp apply_action(socket, :new, _params) do
    assign(socket, :plan, %RecurringPlan{})
  end

  defp apply_action(socket, :edit, %{"id" => id}) do
    assign(socket, :plan, Scheduling.get_recurring_plan!(socket.assigns.current_scope, id))
  end

  # Saving intentionally does not navigate away — the form keeps
  # showing the created series' conflict flags for the owner to
  # review/override afterward (see `PlanFormComponent`).
  @impl true
  def handle_info({PlanFormComponent, {:saved, _plan}}, socket) do
    {:noreply, socket}
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
4	  conflict-aware assignment.
5	
6	  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
7	  """
8	
9	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
10	
11	  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
12	  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
13	  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property
14	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
15	
16	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
17	    AvailabilityBlock,
18	    ConflictDetector,
19	    Job,
20	    Recurrence,
21	    RecurringPlan
22	  }
23	
24	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
25	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User
26	
27	  ## Jobs
28	
29	  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
30	    Job
31	    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
32	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
33	    |> Repo.get!(id)
34	  end
35	
36	  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
37	    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
38	  end
39	
40	  @doc """
41	  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
42	  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
43	  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
44	  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
45	  """
46	  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
47	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
48	    with {:ok, job} <-
49	           %Job{account_id: account_id}
50	           |> Job.changeset(derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))
51	           |> Repo.insert() do
52	      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
53	      {:ok, job}
54	    end
55	  end
56	
57	  # The board's own job form (and a recurring plan's own materialized
58	  # occurrences, via `Recurrence.job_attrs/1`) only ever carry a
59	  # `property_id` — never a `client_id` — so a job created either way
60	  # otherwise saves with `client_id: nil`. That breaks anything reading
61	  # the client straight off the job rather than through its property
62	  # (story 836's invoicing does both a card-on-file charge lookup and
63	  # the invoice's own client label this way), so every job creation
64	  # backfills `client_id` from its property here rather than requiring
65	  # every caller to remember to. A caller that already supplies a
66	  # `client_id` (fixtures with only a client on hand, no property) is
67	  # left alone.
68	  defp derive_client_id(account_id, attrs) do
69	    if blank?(fetch_attr(attrs, :client_id)) do
70	      case fetch_attr(attrs, :property_id) do
71	        value when value in [nil, ""] -> attrs
72	        property_id -> put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id)
73	      end
74	    else
75	      attrs
76	    end
77	  end
78	
79	  defp put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id) do
80	    case Repo.get_by(Property, id: property_id, account_id: account_id) do
81	      %Property{client_id: client_id} when not is_nil(client_id) ->
82	        # Match whichever key style (atom or string) `attrs` already
83	        # uses — `Ecto.Changeset.cast/4` raises on a map mixing both.
84	        if Map.has_key?(attrs, :property_id) do
85	          Map.put(attrs, :client_id, client_id)
86	        else
87	          Map.put(attrs, "client_id", client_id)
88	        end
89	
90	      _ ->
91	        attrs
92	    end
93	  end
94	
95	  defp fetch_attr(attrs, key), do: Map.get(attrs, key) || Map.get(attrs, to_string(key))
96	
97	  defp blank?(nil), do: true
98	  defp blank?(""), do: true
99	  defp blank?(_value), do: false
100	
101	  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
102	    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
103	  end
104	
105	  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
106	    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
107	  end
108	
109	  # Deliberately omits `scheduled_date`: a "created" entry's own
110	  # subject label (job → property/client) is enough to identify which
111	  # job this is, and surfacing it here would read as a schedule change
112	  # (`field_changes/1`'s "Scheduled date: ..." line) indistinguishable
113	  # from an actual reschedule recorded later by `update_job/3`.
114	  defp job_created_values(job) do
115	    %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
116	  end
117	
118	  @doc """
119	  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
120	  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
121	  """
122	  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
123	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
124	    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)
125	
126	    Job
127	    |> where(
128	      [j],
129	      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
130	        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
131	    )
132	    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
133	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
134	    |> Repo.all()
135	  end
136	
137	  @doc """
138	  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
139	  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
140	  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
141	  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
142	
143	  `:include_cancelled_ids` (default `[]`) admits specific cancelled
144	  jobs back in anyway — the board's own escape hatch for a cancelled
145	  job that still carries an unacknowledged schedule-change
146	  notification (story 843): the office needs to keep seeing its
147	  ack-status until the cleaner acknowledges, and the escalation check
148	  needs the job rendered at all to ever run. Other callers passing no
149	  opts see the same non-cancelled set as before.
150	  """
151	  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, opts \\ [])
152	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
153	    include_cancelled_ids = Keyword.get(opts, :include_cancelled_ids, [])
154	
155	    Job
156	    |> where(
157	      [j],
158	      j.account_id == ^account_id and
159	        (j.status != :cancelled or j.id in ^include_cancelled_ids)
160	    )
161	    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
162	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
163	    |> Repo.all()
164	  end
165	
166	  @doc """
167	  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
168	  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
169	  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
170	  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
171	  """
172	  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
173	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
174	    with :ok <-
175	           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
176	             scope,
177	             cleaner_id,
178	             job.scheduled_date,
179	             job.start_time,
180	             job.end_time,
181	             exclude_job_id: job.id
182	           ),
183	         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
184	      Recorder.record(
185	        scope,
186	        "job_reassigned",
187	        "Job",
188	        updated.id,
189	        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
190	        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
191	      )
192	
193	      {:ok, updated}
194	    end
195	  end
196	
197	  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
198	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
199	    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
200	      Recorder.record(
201	        scope,
202	        "job_cancelled",
203	        "Job",
204	        updated.id,
205	        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
206	        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
207	      )
208	
209	      {:ok, updated}
210	    end
211	  end
212	
213	  @doc """
214	  Updates a job's schedule and/or price — a reschedule, a price
215	  change, or both, made directly from the board rather than through
216	  `assign_cleaner/3`'s conflict-checked path. Records only the fields
217	  that actually changed to the audit trail, attributed to the caller.
218	  """
219	  def update_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, attrs)
220	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
221	    changeset = Job.changeset(job, derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))
222	
223	    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
224	      record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated)
225	      {:ok, updated}
226	    end
227	  end
228	
229	  @audited_update_fields ~w(scheduled_date start_time end_time agreed_price_cents status)a
230	
231	  defp record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated) do
232	    changed_fields =
233	      changeset.changes
234	      |> Map.keys()
235	      |> Enum.filter(&(&1 in @audited_update_fields))
236	
237	    if changed_fields != [] do
238	      Recorder.record(
239	        scope,
240	        update_action(changed_fields),
241	        "Job",
242	        updated.id,
243	        audit_snapshot(job, changed_fields),
244	        audit_snapshot(updated, changed_fields)
245	      )
246	    end
247	  end
248	
249	  defp update_action(changed_fields) do
250	    cond do
251	      Enum.any?(changed_fields, &(&1 in [:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])) ->
252	        "job_rescheduled"
253	
254	      :agreed_price_cents in changed_fields ->
255	        "job_price_changed"
256	
257	      true ->
258	        "job_updated"
259	    end
260	  end
261	
262	  defp audit_snapshot(job, fields),
263	    do: Map.new(fields, &{to_string(&1), audit_value(Map.get(job, &1))})
264	
265	  defp audit_value(%Date{} = value), do: to_string(value)
266	  defp audit_value(%Time{} = value), do: to_string(value)
267	  defp audit_value(value), do: value
268	
269	  @doc """
270	  Removes a job from the board without hard-deleting its row — the
271	  row (and any audit entries already about it) stays resolvable for
272	  the trail. Distinct from `cancel_job/2`: this is the office
273	  correcting a mistaken entry rather than calling off an appointment,
274	  so it's recorded as "deleted" rather than "cancelled" and never
275	  notifies the assigned cleaner.
276	  """
277	  def delete_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
278	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
279	    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
280	      Recorder.record(
281	        scope,
282	        "job_deleted",
283	        "Job",
284	        updated.id,
285	        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
286	        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
287	      )
288	
289	      {:ok, updated}
290	    end
291	  end
292	
293	  ## Recurring plans
294	
295	  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
296	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
297	    RecurringPlan
298	    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
299	    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
300	    |> Repo.get!(id)
301	  end
302	
303	  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
304	    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
305	  end
306	
307	  @doc """
308	  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
309	  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
310	  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
311	  """
312	  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
313	    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
314	  end
315	
316	  @doc """
317	  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
318	  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
319	  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
320	  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
321	  """
322	  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
323	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
324	    Repo.transact(fn ->
325	      with {:ok, plan} <-
326	             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
327	             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
328	             |> Repo.insert() do
329	        jobs =
330	          plan
331	          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
332	          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
333	            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs, actor: :system)
334	            job
335	          end)
336	
337	        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
338	      end
339	    end)
340	  end
341	
342	  ## Availability blocks
343	
344	  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
345	    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
346	  end
347	
348	  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
349	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
350	    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
351	    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
352	    |> Repo.insert()
353	  end
354	
355	  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)
356	
357	  @doc """
358	  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
359	  assignment pickers.
360	  """
361	  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
362	    scope
363	    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
364	    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
365	  end
366	
367	  @doc """
368	  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
369	  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
370	  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
371	  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
372	  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
373	  through.
374	  """
375	  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
376	      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
377	    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
378	         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
379	      {:ok, user}
380	    end
381	  end
382	
383	  @doc """
384	  Fetches a single cleaner by id, for their detail page. Draws from
385	  the same membership list as `list_cleaners/1`, so a user who isn't
386	  a member of this account can't be looked up here either. Raises if
387	  not found.
388	  """
389	  def get_cleaner!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
390	    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(id)
391	
392	    scope
393	    |> list_cleaners()
394	    |> Enum.find(&(&1.id == cleaner_id))
395	    |> case do
396	      nil -> raise Ecto.NoResultsError, queryable: User
397	      cleaner -> cleaner
398	    end
399	  end
400	
401	  @doc """
402	  Lists a cleaner's time-off blocks for their detail page, soonest

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan
  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
  """
  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))
           |> Repo.insert() do
      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  # The board's own job form (and a recurring plan's own materialized
  # occurrences, via `Recurrence.job_attrs/1`) only ever carry a
  # `property_id` — never a `client_id` — so a job created either way
  # otherwise saves with `client_id: nil`. That breaks anything reading
  # the client straight off the job rather than through its property
  # (story 836's invoicing does both a card-on-file charge lookup and
  # the invoice's own client label this way), so every job creation
  # backfills `client_id` from its property here rather than requiring
  # every caller to remember to. A caller that already supplies a
  # `client_id` (fixtures with only a client on hand, no property) is
  # left alone.
  defp derive_client_id(account_id, attrs) do
    if blank?(fetch_attr(attrs, :client_id)) do
      case fetch_attr(attrs, :property_id) do
        value when value in [nil, ""] -> attrs
        property_id -> put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id)
      end
    else
      attrs
    end
  end

  defp put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Property, id: property_id, account_id: account_id) do
      %Property{client_id: client_id} when not is_nil(client_id) ->
        # Match whichever key style (atom or string) `attrs` already
        # uses — `Ecto.Changeset.cast/4` raises on a map mixing both.
        if Map.has_key?(attrs, :property_id) do
          Map.put(attrs, :client_id, client_id)
        else
          Map.put(attrs, "client_id", client_id)
        end

      _ ->
        attrs
    end
  end

  defp fetch_attr(attrs, key), do: Map.get(attrs, key) || Map.get(attrs, to_string(key))

  defp blank?(nil), do: true
  defp blank?(""), do: true
  defp blank?(_value), do: false

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  # Deliberately omits `scheduled_date`: a "created" entry's own
  # subject label (job → property/client) is enough to identify which
  # job this is, and surfacing it here would read as a schedule change
  # (`field_changes/1`'s "Scheduled date: ..." line) indistinguishable
  # from an actual reschedule recorded later by `update_job/3`.
  defp job_created_values(job) do
    %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.

  `:include_cancelled_ids` (default `[]`) admits specific cancelled
  jobs back in anyway — the board's own escape hatch for a cancelled
  job that still carries an unacknowledged schedule-change
  notification (story 843): the office needs to keep seeing its
  ack-status until the cleaner acknowledges, and the escalation check
  needs the job rendered at all to ever run. Other callers passing no
  opts see the same non-cancelled set as before.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    include_cancelled_ids = Keyword.get(opts, :include_cancelled_ids, [])

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and
        (j.status != :cancelled or j.id in ^include_cancelled_ids)
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a job's schedule and/or price — a reschedule, a price
  change, or both, made directly from the board rather than through
  `assign_cleaner/3`'s conflict-checked path. Records only the fields
  that actually changed to the audit trail, attributed to the caller.
  """
  def update_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset = Job.changeset(job, derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @audited_update_fields ~w(scheduled_date start_time end_time agreed_price_cents status)a

  defp record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated) do
    changed_fields =
      changeset.changes
      |> Map.keys()
      |> Enum.filter(&(&1 in @audited_update_fields))

    if changed_fields != [] do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        update_action(changed_fields),
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        audit_snapshot(job, changed_fields),
        audit_snapshot(updated, changed_fields)
      )
    end
  end

  defp update_action(changed_fields) do
    cond do
      Enum.any?(changed_fields, &(&1 in [:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])) ->
        "job_rescheduled"

      :agreed_price_cents in changed_fields ->
        "job_price_changed"

      true ->
        "job_updated"
    end
  end

  defp audit_snapshot(job, fields),
    do: Map.new(fields, &{to_string(&1), audit_value(Map.get(job, &1))})

  defp audit_value(%Date{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(%Time{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(value), do: value

  @doc """
  Removes a job from the board without hard-deleting its row — the
  row (and any audit entries already about it) stays resolvable for
  the trail. Distinct from `cancel_job/2`: this is the office
  correcting a mistaken entry rather than calling off an appointment,
  so it's recorded as "deleted" rather than "cancelled" and never
  notifies the assigned cleaner.
  """
  def delete_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_deleted",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs, actor: :system)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a single cleaner by id, for their detail page. Draws from
  the same membership list as `list_cleaners/1`, so a user who isn't
  a member of this account can't be looked up here either. Raises if
  not found.
  """
  def get_cleaner!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(id)

    scope
    |> list_cleaners()
    |> Enum.find(&(&1.id == cleaner_id))
    |> case do
      nil -> raise Ecto.NoResultsError, queryable: User
      cleaner -> cleaner
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists a cleaner's time-off blocks for their detail page, soonest
  first.
  """
  def list_availability_blocks(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(cleaner_id)

    AvailabilityBlock
    |> where([b], b.account_id == ^account_id and b.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id)
    |> order_by([b], asc: b.date)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists a cleaner's upcoming (today or later, non-cancelled) jobs for
  their detail page, soonest first.
  """
  def list_upcoming_jobs_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(cleaner_id)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        j.status != :cancelled and j.scheduled_date >= ^Date.utc_today()
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_integer(id), do: id
  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_binary(id), do: String.to_integer(id)

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Curated bridge from BDD specs into in-app state.

  The only module that may dep on `CleanerCrm` from inside the spex test
  tree. Declared as its own top-level Boundary so the spec boundary
  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.

  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
  """

  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]

  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
            [
              CleanerCrm.Clients,
              CleanerCrm.Scheduling
            ]}

  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
    user
  end

  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
  #
  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false,
          email: "client#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    client
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    attrs = Enum.into(attrs, %{})
    start_time = Map.get(attrs, :start_time, ~T[09:00:00])

    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled,
          scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
          start_time: start_time,
          # Some specs override `start_time` alone (e.g. pinning it to a
          # lead-time boundary) without overriding `end_time` — a fixed
          # `~T[11:00:00]` default would then land before an overridden
          # start_time and fail the "end after start" changeset check.
          end_time: default_end_time(start_time)
        })
      )

    # Notifications (story 837) — the automatic reminder trigger is a
    # periodic Oban-cron scan in production (see the background-jobs
    # ADR); nothing about creating a job through this fixture would
    # otherwise run that scan within a spec's lifetime. Running it here
    # is a no-op for every job outside its owning account's configured
    # lead-time window (and a no-op entirely for accounts that never
    # configured reminders), so it's safe for every other story's jobs
    # while making story 837's own boundary-timed fixtures deterministic.
    CleanerCrm.Notifications.send_due_reminders()

    job
  end

  # `given_` blocks bind `scope` from `user_scope_fixture/1` *before*
  # `account_fixture/2` creates the account, so it never carries an
  # `active_account_id` — every fixture below that scopes a context
  # call by account needs to resolve it from the user's membership at
  # call time instead of trusting the scope it was handed.
  defp scoped_to_account(%CleanerCrm.Users.Scope{active_account_id: nil, user: user} = scope) do
    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(user.id) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  defp scoped_to_account(scope), do: scope

  # Two hours after `start_time`, unless that would wrap past midnight
  # (into an earlier clock time), in which case the day just ends there.
  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, 2 * 3600, :second)
    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

  def job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)
    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })
      )

    invoice
  end

  # Time tracking (story 838) — a resolved clock-in/out record for a
  # job.
  #
  # Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  # 838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job). Scenarios whose subject is a downstream pay
  # calculation (hourly vs. piece-rate, running pay-period totals,
  # payroll CSV export) seed the resolved time entry directly here
  # instead of re-driving the clock-in/out flow every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, time_entry} =
      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })
      )

    time_entry
  end

  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story836.Criterion7153Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 836 — Invoice completed jobs and collect payment
  Criterion 7153 — Completing a job generates its invoice
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "marking a job complete generates its invoice" do
    scenario "completing a job generates its invoice" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a scheduled job has an agreed price of $150", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
            status: :scheduled
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the cleaner marks the job complete", context do
        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        job_live
        |> element("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :job_live, job_live)}
      end

      then_ "the job is shown as complete to the cleaner", context do
        assert render(context.job_live) =~ "Complete"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "an invoice for $150 appears in the owner's billing queue", context do
        {:ok, _invoices_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/invoices")

        assert html =~ context.client.name
        assert html =~ "$150.00"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story833.Criterion7143Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 833 — Schedule recurring cleaning plans with series-wide conflict detection
  Criterion 7143 — A recurring plan generates a job for every occurrence in
  its series (weekly, biweekly, or monthly), not just the first.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

  spex "a recurring plan generates the full series of jobs" do
    scenario "weekly plan generates the full series" do
      given_(:logged_in_owner_with_account)

      given_ "a client \"Jamie Rivera\" with a property exists", context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Jamie Rivera")

        property_path =
          create_property(context.conn, client_path, %{service_address: "12 Oak Lane"})

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           client_path: client_path,
           property_id: id_from_path(property_path)
         })}
      end

      given_ "a cleaner \"Alex Morgan\" is available for assignment", context do
        cleaner_path = create_cleaner(context.conn, "Alex Morgan")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :cleaner_id, id_from_path(cleaner_path))}
      end

      given_ "the owner creates a weekly cleaning plan for a property running for 8 weeks",
             context do
        {:ok, plan_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule/plans/new")

        plan_live
        |> form("[data-test='plan-form']",
          plan: %{
            property_id: context.property_id,
            cleaner_id: context.cleaner_id,
            recurrence: "weekly",
            start_date: Date.to_iso8601(first_visit_date()),
            occurrence_count: 8
          }
        )
        |> render_change()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :plan_live, plan_live)}
      end

      when_ "the plan is saved", context do
        context.plan_live
        |> element("[data-test='save-plan-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "8 jobs are created, one on each scheduled date", context do
        {:ok, _board_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        assert html =~ "8 jobs scheduled"
        assert length(Regex.scan(~r/data-test="job-card"/, html)) == 8

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp first_visit_date, do: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)
  defp id_from_path(path), do: path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()

  defp create_client(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='client-form']", client: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_property(conn, client_path, attrs) do
    "/clients/" <> client_id = client_path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_cleaner(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/schedule/cleaners/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='cleaner-form']", cleaner: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end
end
