defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story846.Criterion7196Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 846 — Keep the same cleaner on the same home
  Criterion 7196 — Owner sets a preferred cleaner on a recurring plan:
  when creating a recurring plan for a property, the owner designates a
  preferred cleaner, and the plan's own generated visit is assigned to
  that cleaner.

  Assumes `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent` (opened from
  `/schedule/plans/new`, per story 833's own specs) exposes a
  `[data-test='plan-form']` whose `cleaner_id` field designates the
  plan's preferred cleaner — `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan`
  "records the client's preferred cleaner" per its architecture spec —
  and a `[data-test='save-plan-button']` that saves the plan and
  materializes its occurrence(s) immediately, per criterion 7143.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

  spex "the owner designates a preferred cleaner when creating a recurring plan" do
    scenario "owner sets a preferred cleaner on a recurring plan" do
      given_(:logged_in_owner_with_account)

      given_ "a client \"Jamie Rivera\" with a property exists", context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Jamie Rivera")

        property_path =
          create_property(context.conn, client_path, %{service_address: "12 Oak Lane"})

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           client_path: client_path,
           property_id: id_from_path(property_path)
         })}
      end

      given_ "a cleaner \"Alex Morgan\" is available for assignment", context do
        cleaner_path = create_cleaner(context.conn, "Alex Morgan")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :cleaner_id, id_from_path(cleaner_path))}
      end

      when_ "the owner creates a recurring plan and sets Alex Morgan as the preferred cleaner",
            context do
        {:ok, plan_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule/plans/new")

        plan_live
        |> form("[data-test='plan-form']",
          plan: %{
            property_id: context.property_id,
            cleaner_id: context.cleaner_id,
            recurrence: "weekly",
            start_date: Date.to_iso8601(first_visit_date()),
            occurrence_count: 1
          }
        )
        |> render_change()

        plan_live
        |> element("[data-test='save-plan-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the plan's generated visit is assigned to the preferred cleaner, Alex Morgan",
            context do
        {:ok, board_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        [job_id] = job_ids(html)

        assert has_element?(
                 board_live,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{context.cleaner_id}'] [data-test='job-#{job_id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp first_visit_date, do: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)
  defp id_from_path(path), do: path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()

  defp job_ids(html) do
    ~r/data-test="job-([0-9a-f-]+)"/
    |> Regex.scan(html)
    |> Enum.map(fn [_, id] -> id end)
    |> Enum.uniq()
  end

  defp create_client(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='client-form']", client: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_property(conn, client_path, attrs) do
    "/clients/" <> client_id = client_path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_cleaner(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/schedule/cleaners/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='cleaner-form']", cleaner: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTrackingTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  setup do
    owner = user_fixture()
    owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(owner_scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})

    cleaner = user_fixture()
    {:ok, _member} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(owner_scope, cleaner.id, account.id, :member)

    scope = %{owner_scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}

    {:ok, client} = Clients.create_client(scope, %{name: "A Client"})

    %{scope: scope, cleaner: cleaner, client: client}
  end

  defp job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs) do
    {:ok, job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
          status: :scheduled
        })
      )

    job
  end

  describe "clock_in/2 and clock_out/2" do
    test "rejects a cleaner who isn't assigned to the job", %{
      scope: scope,
      client: client,
      cleaner: assigned_cleaner
    } do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, assigned_cleaner, %{})
      someone_else_scope = %{scope | user: user_fixture()}

      assert {:error, :not_assigned} = TimeTracking.clock_in(someone_else_scope, job)
    end

    test "clocks in and out, recording worked time", %{
      scope: scope,
      client: client,
      cleaner: cleaner
    } do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, %{})
      cleaner_scope = %{scope | user: cleaner}

      assert {:ok, entry} = TimeTracking.clock_in(cleaner_scope, job)
      assert entry.clocked_out_at == nil

      assert {:ok, resolved} = TimeTracking.clock_out(cleaner_scope, job)
      assert resolved.clocked_out_at != nil
    end

    test "refuses a second clock-in while already clocked in elsewhere", %{
      scope: scope,
      client: client,
      cleaner: cleaner
    } do
      job_a = job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, %{})
      job_b = job_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, %{})
      cleaner_scope = %{scope | user: cleaner}

      assert {:ok, _entry} = TimeTracking.clock_in(cleaner_scope, job_a)

end

  @doc "Marks a required item skipped instead of done, with a reason."
  def skip_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{} = item, reason) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.skip_changeset(reason) |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc """
  The required items still blocking completion: unchecked and not
  skipped. Empty means the checklist is ready to complete.
  """
  def incomplete_required_items(%Checklist{items: items}) do
    Enum.filter(items, &(&1.required and not &1.checked and not &1.skipped))
  end

  @doc """
  Completes a job's checklist: refused with the still-incomplete
  required items when any remain; otherwise the checklist is stamped
  done, scored, and the job itself is marked completed.
  """
  def complete_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Checklist{} = checklist) do
    case incomplete_required_items(checklist) do
      [] -> do_complete_job(scope, checklist)
      incomplete -> {:error, {:incomplete_required_tasks, incomplete}}
    end
  end

  defp do_complete_job(scope, checklist) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, completed} <- mark_checklist_completed(checklist),
           {:ok, _job} <- mark_job_completed(scope, completed.job_id) do
        {:ok, completed}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp mark_checklist_completed(checklist) do
    checklist
    |> Checklist.changeset(%{
      completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
      quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
    })
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp current_path_last_segment(session) do

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Room-by-room checklists instantiated per job, before/after photo
4	  proof, incident reports (damage, missing items, unsafe conditions),
5	  and the scorecards that aggregate a cleaner's completed jobs.
6	
7	  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
8	  """
9	
10	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
11	
12	  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
13	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
14	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
15	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
16	
17	  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.{
18	    Checklist,
19	    ChecklistItem,
20	    ChecklistTemplate,
21	    IncidentReport,
22	    Photo,
23	    Scorecard
24	  }
25	
26	  ## Checklist templates
27	
28	  def list_checklist_templates(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
29	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
30	    ChecklistTemplate
31	    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
32	    |> order_by([t], asc: t.name)
33	    |> preload(:property)
34	    |> Repo.all()
35	  end
36	
37	  def get_checklist_template!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
38	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
39	    ChecklistTemplate
40	    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
41	    |> preload(:property)
42	    |> Repo.get!(id)
43	  end
44	
45	  def change_checklist_template(%Scope{}, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template, attrs \\ %{}) do
46	    ChecklistTemplate.changeset(template, attrs)
47	  end
48	
49	  def create_checklist_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
50	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
51	    %ChecklistTemplate{account_id: account_id}
52	    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
53	    |> Repo.insert()
54	  end
55	
56	  def update_checklist_template(
57	        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
58	        %ChecklistTemplate{} = template,
59	        attrs
60	      )
61	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
62	    template
63	    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
64	    |> Repo.update()
65	  end
66	
67	  ## Checklists
68	
69	  @doc """
70	  Instantiates a job's checklist from a template, copying its
71	  room/task/required lines down as the job's own checklist items.
72	  """
73	  def instantiate_checklist(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template) do
74	    create_checklist(scope, job, ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), template_id: template.id)
75	  end
76	
77	  @doc """
78	  Creates a job's checklist from `items` — each a `%{task:, required:}`
79	  map, optionally carrying `room:` — in the order given. Every
80	  checklist item starts unchecked and un-skipped.
81	
82	  Called with an empty `items` list and no explicit `template_id` in
83	  `opts`, this looks for a `ChecklistTemplate` on the job's property
84	  and instantiates from it instead of leaving the checklist empty.
85	  This is what lets `FieldLive.Job`'s lazy
86	  `create_checklist(scope, job, [])` — called the first time a
87	  cleaner opens a job with no checklist yet — pick up a real,
88	  room-by-room checklist once the office has built one for the
89	  property, without that caller needing to know templates exist.
90	  """
91	  def create_checklist(
92	        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
93	        %Job{id: job_id} = job,
94	        items,
95	        opts \\ []
96	      )
97	      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
98	    {items, opts} = apply_property_template(scope, job, items, opts)
99	
100	    Repo.transact(fn ->
101	      with {:ok, checklist} <-
102	             %Checklist{account_id: account_id}
103	             |> Checklist.changeset(%{job_id: job_id, checklist_template_id: opts[:template_id]})
104	             |> Repo.insert() do
105	        item_structs =
106	          items
107	          |> Enum.with_index()
108	          |> Enum.map(fn {attrs, position} ->
109	            insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position)
110	          end)
111	
112	        {:ok, %{checklist | items: item_structs}}
113	      end
114	    end)
115	  end
116	
117	  defp apply_property_template(_scope, _job, items, opts) when items != [], do: {items, opts}
118	
119	  defp apply_property_template(scope, %Job{property_id: property_id}, [], opts) do
120	    cond do
121	      # `opts[:template_id]` is a keyword-list lookup (`Access.get/2`), which
122	      # isn't allowed in a guard — checked here in the body instead.
123	      not is_nil(opts[:template_id]) -> {[], opts}
124	      is_nil(property_id) -> {[], opts}
125	      true -> apply_found_template(scope, property_id, opts)
126	    end
127	  end
128	
129	  defp apply_found_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, property_id, opts) do
130	    case find_template_for_property(account_id, property_id) do
131	      nil ->
132	        {[], opts}
133	
134	      template ->
135	        {ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), Keyword.put(opts, :template_id, template.id)}
136	    end
137	  end
138	
139	  defp find_template_for_property(account_id, property_id) do
140	    ChecklistTemplate
141	    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id and t.property_id == ^property_id)
142	    |> order_by([t], desc: t.updated_at)
143	    |> limit(1)
144	    |> Repo.one()
145	  end
146	
147	  defp insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position) do
148	    params =
149	      attrs
150	      |> Map.new(fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)
151	      |> Map.put("checklist_id", checklist.id)
152	      |> Map.put_new("position", position)
153	
154	    %ChecklistItem{}
155	    |> ChecklistItem.changeset(params)
156	    |> Repo.insert!()
157	  end
158	
159	  @doc """
160	  Fetches a job's checklist with its items and their photos
161	  preloaded, or `nil` if the job has none yet.
162	  """
163	  def get_checklist_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id})

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality do
  @moduledoc """
  Room-by-room checklists instantiated per job, before/after photo
  proof, incident reports (damage, missing items, unsafe conditions),
  and the scorecards that aggregate a cleaner's completed jobs.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.{
    Checklist,
    ChecklistItem,
    ChecklistTemplate,
    IncidentReport,
    Photo,
    Scorecard
  }

  ## Checklist templates

  def list_checklist_templates(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.name)
    |> preload(:property)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_checklist_template!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(:property)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_checklist_template(%Scope{}, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template, attrs \\ %{}) do
    ChecklistTemplate.changeset(template, attrs)
  end

  def create_checklist_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %ChecklistTemplate{account_id: account_id}
    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def update_checklist_template(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %ChecklistTemplate{} = template,
        attrs
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    template
    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  ## Checklists

  @doc """
  Instantiates a job's checklist from a template, copying its
  room/task/required lines down as the job's own checklist items.
  """
  def instantiate_checklist(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template) do
    create_checklist(scope, job, ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), template_id: template.id)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist from `items` — each a `%{task:, required:}`
  map, optionally carrying `room:` — in the order given. Every
  checklist item starts unchecked and un-skipped.

  Called with an empty `items` list and no explicit `template_id` in
  `opts`, this looks for a `ChecklistTemplate` on the job's property
  and instantiates from it instead of leaving the checklist empty.
  This is what lets `FieldLive.Job`'s lazy
  `create_checklist(scope, job, [])` — called the first time a
  cleaner opens a job with no checklist yet — pick up a real,
  room-by-room checklist once the office has built one for the
  property, without that caller needing to know templates exist.
  """
  def create_checklist(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        %Job{id: job_id} = job,
        items,
        opts \\ []
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    {items, opts} = apply_property_template(scope, job, items, opts)

    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             %Checklist{account_id: account_id}
             |> Checklist.changeset(%{job_id: job_id, checklist_template_id: opts[:template_id]})
             |> Repo.insert() do
        item_structs =
          items
          |> Enum.with_index()
          |> Enum.map(fn {attrs, position} ->
            insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position)
          end)

        {:ok, %{checklist | items: item_structs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp apply_property_template(_scope, _job, items, opts) when items != [], do: {items, opts}

  defp apply_property_template(scope, %Job{property_id: property_id}, [], opts) do
    cond do
      # `opts[:template_id]` is a keyword-list lookup (`Access.get/2`), which
      # isn't allowed in a guard — checked here in the body instead.
      not is_nil(opts[:template_id]) -> {[], opts}
      is_nil(property_id) -> {[], opts}
      true -> apply_found_template(scope, property_id, opts)
    end
  end

  defp apply_found_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, property_id, opts) do
    case find_template_for_property(account_id, property_id) do
      nil ->
        {[], opts}

      template ->
        {ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), Keyword.put(opts, :template_id, template.id)}
    end
  end

  defp find_template_for_property(account_id, property_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id and t.property_id == ^property_id)
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.updated_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  defp insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position) do
    params =
      attrs
      |> Map.new(fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)
      |> Map.put("checklist_id", checklist.id)
      |> Map.put_new("position", position)

    %ChecklistItem{}
    |> ChecklistItem.changeset(params)
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a job's checklist with its items and their photos
  preloaded, or `nil` if the job has none yet.
  """
  def get_checklist_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Checklist
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id and c.job_id == ^job_id)
    |> preload(items: :photos)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  @doc """
  Groups a checklist's items by room, in the order each room first
  appears. Items with no room (a flat, unrouted checklist) are
  grouped under `nil`.
  """
  def group_by_room(%Checklist{items: items}) do
    rooms = Enum.uniq_by(items, & &1.room) |> Enum.map(& &1.room)
    grouped = Enum.group_by(items, & &1.room)
    Enum.map(rooms, &{&1, Map.fetch!(grouped, &1)})
  end

  @doc "`{checked_count, total_count}` across a checklist's items."
  def progress(%Checklist{items: items}), do: {Enum.count(items, & &1.checked), length(items)}

  @doc """
  Toggles a checklist item's checked state. Checking an item clears
  any prior skip.
  """
  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{checked: true} = item) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.uncheck_changeset() |> Repo.update()
  end

  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{} = item) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update()
  end

  schema "recurring_plans" do
    field :recurrence, Ecto.Enum, values: [:weekly, :biweekly, :monthly]
    field :start_date, :date
    field :occurrence_count, :integer
    field :start_time, :time, default: ~T[09:00:00]
    field :end_time, :time, default: ~T[11:00:00]

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(property_id cleaner_id recurrence start_date occurrence_count start_time end_time)a

  @doc """
  Changeset for the fully-specified plan a save requires.
  """
  def changeset(plan, attrs) do
    plan
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:property_id, :recurrence, :start_date, :occurrence_count])
    |> validate_number(:occurrence_count, greater_than: 0)
  end

  @doc """
  Changeset for the live preview as the owner fills in the form —
  every field is optional so the conflict list can update incrementally
  as soon as enough of them are present, well before the plan is valid
  enough to save.
  """
  def preview_changeset(plan, attrs) do
    cast(plan, attrs, @fields)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence do
  @moduledoc """
  Generates the dates for a plan's series from its cadence.

  Project-local, calendar-date arithmetic (see the recurrence ADR) —
  no RRULE library, no virtual occurrences. `:weekly` steps 7 days,
  `:biweekly` 14, `:monthly` 28 (a fixed 4-week cadence, not a calendar
  month, so the weekday never drifts).

  TODO: the recurrence ADR calls for materializing against each
  account's IANA timezone (via `tzdata`) so visits stay pinned to local
  wall-clock across DST, plus a rolling 12-week horizon extended by a
  daily Oban job. Neither is implemented yet — dates here are naive
  and every plan is materialized in full up front, bounded only by its
  own `occurrence_count`.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan

  @step_days %{weekly: 7, biweekly: 14, monthly: 28}

  @doc """
  Returns a list of `%{index:, date:}` maps, one per occurrence, in
  series order starting at 1. `nil` if the plan is missing any of the
  fields a series needs.
  """
  def occurrences(%RecurringPlan{
        recurrence: recurrence,
        start_date: %Date{} = start_date,
        occurrence_count: count
      })
      when recurrence in [:weekly, :biweekly, :monthly] and is_integer(count) and count > 0 do
    step = Map.fetch!(@step_days, recurrence)

    for index <- 1..count do
      %{index: index, date: Date.add(start_date, (index - 1) * step)}
    end
  end

  def occurrences(_incomplete_plan), do: []

  @doc """
  Job attribute maps ready for `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job/2`, one
  per occurrence.
  """
  def job_attrs(%RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    Enum.map(occurrences(plan), fn %{date: date} ->
      %{
        property_id: plan.property_id,
        cleaner_id: plan.cleaner_id,
        recurring_plan_id: plan.id,
        scheduled_date: date,
        start_time: plan.start_time,
        end_time: plan.end_time
      }
    end)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent do @moduledoc """ Create or edit a recurring plan, with series-wide conflict detection that updates live as the owner fills in the form. Saving a plan never blocks on conflicts — every occurrence still gets created and (if a preferred cleaner is set) still assigned to them. Conflicts stay visible after a save so the owner can keep reviewing/overriding them; this component intentionally does not navigate away on its own after saving (see `PlanLive`). ## Assigns | Assign | Type | Required | Description | |---------------|---------------------|----------|-------------------------------------------------| | id | string | yes | LiveComponent DOM id | | current_scope | `Scope.t()` | yes | caller scope, used for all context calls | | action | `:new \\| :edit` | yes | which mode the form is in | | plan | `RecurringPlan.t()` | yes | blank `%RecurringPlan{}` for `:new`, loaded for `:edit` | On successful save, sends `{__MODULE__, {:saved, plan}}` to the parent. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component import Ecto.Query, warn: false alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property alias CleanerCrm.Repo alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H"""
<.header>{form_title(@action)} <.form for={@form} id={"#{@id}-form"} data-test="plan-form" phx-target={@myself} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save" > <.input field={@form[:property_id]} type="select" label="Property" prompt="Select a property" options={property_options(@properties)} /> <.input field={@form[:cleaner_id]} type="select" label="Preferred Cleaner" prompt="No preferred cleaner" options={cleaner_options(@cleaners)} /> <.input field={@form[:recurrence]} type="select" label="Recurrence" prompt="Select a cadence" options={[{"Weekly", "weekly"}, {"Biweekly", "biweekly"}, {"Every 4 weeks", "monthly"}]} /> <.input field={@form[:start_date]} type="date" label="Start Date" /> <.input field={@form[:occurrence_count]} type="number" label="Number of Visits" min="1" />
Visit {conflict.index} ({conflict.date}) has a scheduling conflict: {conflict_reason_text( conflict.reason )}. <.button type="button" data-test={"override-conflict-#{conflict.index}"} phx-target={@myself} phx-click="override_conflict" phx-value-index={conflict.index} > Override
<.button type="button" data-test="save-plan-button" phx-target={@myself} phx-click="save" phx-disable-with="Saving..." > Save Plan
""" end @impl true def update(%{plan: plan} = assigns, socket) do changeset = Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(assigns.current_scope, plan, %{}) {:ok, socket |> assign(assigns) |> assign(:overridden, MapSet.new()) |> assign(:properties, list_properties(assigns.current_scope)) |> assign(:cleaners, Scheduling.list_cleaners(assigns.current_scope)) |> assign_form_and_conflicts(changeset)} end @impl true def handle_event("validate", %{"plan" => params}, socket) do changeset = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.plan, params) |> Map.put(:action, :validate) {:noreply, assign_form_and_conflicts(socket, changeset)} end def handle_event("override_conflict", %{"index" => index}, socket) do index = String.to_integer(index) {:noreply, socket |> Phoenix.Component.update(:overridden, &MapSet.put(&1, index)) |> Phoenix.Component.update( :conflicts, &Enum.reject(&1, fn conflict -> conflict.index == index end) )} end # The save button is a plain `phx-click`, not a form submit — the # board's own conflict-review flow drives it that way (see the # spex). It carries no params of its own, so it saves whatever the # last "validate" pass put in the form. def handle_event("save", %{"plan" => params}, socket), do: save_plan(socket, params) def handle_event("save", _params, socket), do: save_plan(socket, socket.assigns.form.params || %{}) defp save_plan(socket, params) do case Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do {:ok, {plan, _jobs}} -> notify_parent({:saved, plan}) changeset = Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.current_scope, plan, %{}) {:noreply, socket |> assign(:plan, plan) |> assign_form_and_conflicts(changeset)} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :plan))} end end defp assign_form_and_conflicts(socket, changeset) do draft = Ecto.Changeset.apply_changes(changeset) conflicts = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Scheduling.preview_conflicts(draft) |> Enum.reject(&MapSet.member?(socket.assigns.overridden, &1.index)) socket |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset, as: :plan)) |> assign(:conflicts, conflicts) end defp notify_parent(msg), do: send(self(), {__MODULE__, msg}) defp list_properties(%{active_account_id: account_id}) do Property |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id) |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address) |> Repo.all() end defp property_options(properties), do: Enum.map(properties, &{&1.service_address, &1.id}) defp cleaner_options(cleaners), do: Enum.map(cleaners, &{&1.name || &1.email, &1.id}) defp conflict_reason_text(:unavailable), do: "the cleaner is unavailable that day" defp conflict_reason_text(:overlap), do: "it overlaps another booking" defp form_title(:new), do: "New Recurring Plan" defp form_title(:edit), do: "Edit Recurring Plan" end

@doc """
  Generates the invoice for a job that's just been marked complete —
  see the moduledoc for where this gets wired in once job completion
  has a real caller.

  Returns `{:error, :no_price}` without creating an invoice, and
  without touching the database at all, when the job has no
  `agreed_price_cents` — e.g. a visit materialized from a
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan` with no price set (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1`). Job completion itself
  must still succeed in that case, so callers should let this error
  through rather than fail the completion on it. There's no dedicated
  "completed jobs missing an invoice" queue today — the office notices
  a missing invoice by comparing the schedule board's completed jobs
  against `list_invoices/1`, or avoids it entirely by pricing the job
  (or its recurring plan) before it's completed.
  """
  def generate_for_job(%Scope{}, %Job{agreed_price_cents: nil}), do: {:error, :no_price}

  def generate_for_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, amount_cents: job.agreed_price_cents, status: :unpaid})
  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing do
  @moduledoc """
  Invoices generated from completed jobs and payment collection via
  card-on-file or a public payment link, with proof-of-work attached
  from `CleanerCrm.Quality` for chargeback defense.

  Per the payments-stripe ADR, an invoice's `status` only ever advances
  on a Stripe webhook confirmation: `charge_card/2` and
  `pay_via_link/2` just submit a PaymentIntent and move the invoice to
  `:charge_pending`; only `receive_webhook/1` marks it `:paid`, or
  reverts it to `:unpaid` on a decline so the owner can retry or send a
  payment link.

  Every function that isn't reached from the public `/pay/:token` or
  `/webhooks/stripe` routes is scoped to the caller's active account —
  those two have no logged-in user to scope against.

  ## Job completion integration point

  No caller generates an invoice automatically yet: job completion
  itself lives in `CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_job/2`
  (`CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job`, which will drive it, doesn't exist
  yet either). Once it does, the natural hook is right there — call
  `generate_for_job/2` with the now-completed job after
  `Quality.complete_job/2` succeeds.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.{Invoice, Payment, ReceiptNotifier, StripeGateway}
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  ## Invoices

  @doc "Lists the account's invoices, most recent first, for the billing queue."
  def list_invoices(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([i], desc: i.inserted_at)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_invoice!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  @doc """
  Looks up an invoice by its public payment-link token. Takes no
  `Scope` — the payer on `/pay/:token` isn't a logged-in user, so the
  token itself (unguessable, unique) is the only access control this
  lookup has.
  """
  def get_invoice_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.payment_token == ^token)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def create_invoice(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Invoice{account_id: account_id}
    |> Invoice.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Generates the invoice for a job that's just been marked complete —
  see the moduledoc for where this gets wired in once job completion
  has a real caller.
  """
  def generate_for_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, amount_cents: job.agreed_price_cents, status: :unpaid})
  end

  ## Payment collection

  @doc """
  Charges the client's card on file for the invoice's full amount.
  Refused with `{:error, :no_card_on_file}` when the client has none.
  """
  def charge_card(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> invoice_client()
    |> submit_and_finalize_charge(invoice, off_session: true, source: "card_on_file")
  end

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{card_on_file: false}, _invoice, _opts),
    do: {:error, :no_card_on_file}

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{} = client, invoice, opts) do
    {source, charge_opts} = Keyword.pop!(opts, :source)

    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           submit_charge(invoice, payment_method_for(client), charge_opts) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, client, intent_id, source)
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Charges the given payment method against the invoice reached via its
  public payment-link token — the `/pay/:token` page's own flow, with
  no card on file and no logged-in payer to scope against.
  """
  def pay_via_link(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <- submit_charge(invoice, payment_method, off_session: false) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, invoice_client(invoice), intent_id, "payment_link")
    end
  end

  defp submit_charge(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method, opts) do
    StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      payment_method: payment_method,
      off_session: Keyword.get(opts, :off_session, false),
      metadata: %{invoice_id: invoice.id}
    })
  end

  # Clients doesn't yet persist a real Stripe payment-method/customer id
  # (only the `card_on_file` flag) — this placeholder stands in until a
  # SetupIntent-backed token is stored. The Test adapter ignores it
  # entirely, and the Live adapter is never exercised without one.
  defp payment_method_for(%Client{id: id}), do: "card_on_file:#{id}"

  defp finalize_charge_submission(%Invoice{} = invoice, client, intent_id, source) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <-
             invoice
             |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: :charge_pending, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id})
             |> Repo.update(),
           {:ok, _payment} <- record_payment(updated, intent_id, source, :pending) do
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
    |> tap(fn
      {:ok, updated} -> send_receipt(client, updated)
      _error -> :ok
    end)
  end

  @doc """
  Generates (or reuses) an invoice's public payment-link token, so the
  owner can share `/pay/:token` with a client who has no card on file.
  """
  def create_payment_link(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> Invoice.changeset(%{payment_token: invoice.payment_token || generate_token()})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)

  defp invoice_client(%Invoice{} = invoice) do
    invoice |> Repo.preload(job: :client) |> then(& &1.job.client)
  end

  defp send_receipt(%Client{email: email}, %Invoice{} = invoice) when is_binary(email) do
    ReceiptNotifier.deliver_receipt(email, invoice)
    :ok
  end

  defp send_receipt(_client, _invoice), do: :ok

  defp record_payment(%Invoice{} = invoice, intent_id, source, status) do
    %Payment{account_id: invoice.account_id, invoice_id: invoice.id}
    |> Payment.changeset(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      status: status,
      provider: "stripe",
      stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id,
      source: source
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Webhook

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request — the
  controller's only touchpoint into this context, so it never sees
  event data it can't trust.
  """
  def receive_webhook(conn) do
    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
      apply_webhook_event(event)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :paid, :succeeded)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :unpaid, :failed)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:ok, :ignored}

  defp find_invoice_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => invoice_id}} when is_binary(invoice_id) ->
        fetch_invoice(invoice_id)

      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) ->
        fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id)

      _ ->
        {:error, :invoice_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice(invoice_id) do
    case Repo.get(Invoice, invoice_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Invoice, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  # `stripe_payment_intent_id` is left as-is on a decline (never
  # cleared) — its presence is what tells `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show`
  # to offer "retry" instead of the initial "charge card" action.
  defp transition_invoice(%Invoice{} = invoice, new_status, payment_status) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <- invoice |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: new_status}) |> Repo.update() do
        update_payment_record(updated, payment_status)
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
  end

  # The `Payment` submitted alongside the charge is normally still
  # `:pending` here and just gets its outcome filled in; a fixture-seeded
  # invoice (no prior `charge_card/2` call) has none, so one is created
  # for the audit trail.
  defp update_payment_record(%Invoice{} = invoice, status) do
    case Repo.get_by(Payment,
           invoice_id: invoice.id,
           stripe_payment_intent_id: invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id
         ) do
      nil -> record_payment(invoice, invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id, "webhook", status)
      payment -> payment |> Payment.changeset(%{status: status}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.Invoice do
  @moduledoc """
  An invoice for a completed job.

  Per the payments-stripe ADR, `status` only ever advances on a Stripe
  webhook confirmation: charging a card or sending a payment link just
  submits a charge and moves the invoice to `:charge_pending`; only the
  webhook marks it `:paid`, and a declined charge reverts it to
  `:unpaid` so the owner can retry or fall back to a payment link.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type status :: :unpaid | :charge_pending | :paid

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          amount_cents: integer() | nil,
          status: status(),
          stripe_payment_intent_id: String.t() | nil,
          payment_token: String.t() | nil,
          job: CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job.t() | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "invoices" do
    field :amount_cents, :integer
    field :amount, :decimal, virtual: true
    field :status, Ecto.Enum, values: [:unpaid, :charge_pending, :paid], default: :unpaid
    field :stripe_payment_intent_id, :string
    field :payment_token, :string

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(job_id amount amount_cents status stripe_payment_intent_id payment_token)a

  def changeset(invoice, attrs) do
    invoice
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:job_id])
    |> put_amount_cents()
    |> validate_number(:amount_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> unique_constraint(:payment_token)
  end

  # `amount` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the money-handling
  # ADR); rounded half-up and stored as `amount_cents` — the only column
  # ever persisted. Callers that already have cents (e.g. copying a job's
  # `agreed_price_cents`) pass `amount_cents` directly and skip this.
  defp put_amount_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :amount) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :amount_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.DataCase do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines the setup for tests requiring
  access to the application's data layer.

  You may define functions here to be used as helpers in
  your tests.

  Finally, if the test case interacts with the database,
  we enable the SQL sandbox, so changes done to the database
  are reverted at the end of every test. If you are using
  PostgreSQL, you can even run database tests asynchronously
  by setting `use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true`, although
  this option is not recommended for other databases.
  """

  use ExUnit.CaseTemplate

  using do
    quote do
      alias CleanerCrm.Repo

      import Ecto
      import Ecto.Changeset
      import Ecto.Query
      import CleanerCrmTest.DataCase
    end
  end

  setup tags do
    CleanerCrmTest.DataCase.setup_sandbox(tags)
    :ok
  end

  @doc """
  Sets up the sandbox based on the test tags.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{Recurrence, RecurringPlan}

  describe "job_attrs/1" do
    test "carries the plan's agreed_price_cents onto every occurrence" do
      plan = %RecurringPlan{
        id: Ecto.UUID.generate(),
        property_id: Ecto.UUID.generate(),
        cleaner_id: nil,
        recurrence: :weekly,
        start_date: ~D[2026-08-03],

      assert length(attrs) == 3
      assert Enum.all?(attrs, &(&1.agreed_price_cents == 15_000))
    end

    # visits with no price either, and completing one of those jobs must
    # not crash invoice generation (see `CleanerCrm.BillingTest`).

      }

      attrs = Recurrence.job_attrs(plan)

      assert length(attrs) == 2
      assert Enum.all?(attrs, &(&1.agreed_price_cents == nil))
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.BillingTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.Invoice
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  setup do
    owner = user_fixture()
    owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(owner_scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})
    scope = %{owner_scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}

    {:ok, client} = Clients.create_client(scope, %{name: "A Client"})

    %{scope: scope, client: client}
  end

  defp job_fixture(scope, client, attrs) do
    {:ok, job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
          status: :scheduled
        })
      )

    job
  end

  describe "generate_for_job/2" do
    test "generates an invoice for the job's agreed price", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, %{agreed_price_cents: 15_000})

      assert {:ok, %Invoice{} = invoice} = Billing.generate_for_job(scope, job)
      assert invoice.amount_cents == 15_000
      assert invoice.job_id == job.id
    end

    # Regression: a job materialized from a recurring plan with no price
    # (e.g. `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1` on an unpriced
    # plan) has `agreed_price_cents: nil`. Generating its invoice used to
    # attempt an insert with a `nil` `amount_cents` and crash on the
    # column's NOT NULL constraint — completing the job must still
    # succeed, so this must return an error tuple, never raise.
    test "skips invoice creation and returns {:error, :no_price} for a nil-priced job, without touching the database",
         %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, %{agreed_price_cents: nil})

      assert {:error, :no_price} = Billing.generate_for_job(scope, job)
      assert Billing.list_invoices(scope) == []
    end
  end

  describe "create_invoice/2" do
    test "refuses a nil amount_cents with a changeset error instead of crashing", %{
      scope: scope,
      client: client
    } do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, %{agreed_price_cents: nil})

      assert {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} =
               Billing.create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, status: :unpaid})

      assert %{amount_cents: ["can't be blank"]} = errors_on(changeset)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines the test case to be used by
  tests that require setting up a connection.

  Such tests rely on `Phoenix.ConnTest` and also
  import other functionality to make it easier
  to build common data structures and query the data layer.

  Finally, if the test case interacts with the database,
  we enable the SQL sandbox, so changes done to the database
  are reverted at the end of every test. If you are using
  PostgreSQL, you can even run database tests asynchronously
  by setting `use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true`, although
  this option is not recommended for other databases.
  """

  use ExUnit.CaseTemplate

  using do
    quote do
      # The default endpoint for testing
      @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

      # Import conveniences for testing with connections
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.ConnTest
      import CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase
    end
  end

  setup tags do
    CleanerCrmTest.DataCase.setup_sandbox(tags)
    {:ok, conn: Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()}
  end

  @doc """
  Setup helper that registers and logs in users.

      setup :register_and_log_in_user

  It stores an updated connection and a registered user in the
  test context.
  """
  def register_and_log_in_user(%{conn: conn} = context) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = CleanerCrm.Users.Scope.for_user(user)

    opts =
      context
      |> Map.take([:token_authenticated_at])
      |> Enum.into([])

    %{conn: log_in_user(conn, user, opts), user: user, scope: scope}
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the given `user` into the `conn`.

  It returns an updated `conn`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, opts \\ []) do
    token = CleanerCrm.Users.generate_user_session_token(user)

    maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, opts[:token_authenticated_at])

    conn
    |> Phoenix.ConnTest.init_test_session(%{})
    |> Plug.Conn.put_session(:user_token, token)
  end

  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(_token, nil), do: nil

  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) do
    CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistComponentTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp owner_scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{user: user, scope: %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}}
  end

  # Regression for the accepted issue: completing a job with no agreed
  # price crashed invoice generation on the `invoices.amount_cents` NOT
  # NULL constraint. An unpriced recurring plan materializes visits
  # with no price (`CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1`), so
  # this drives that exact real-usage path end to end: create such a
  # plan, then complete the job it generated through the live UI.
  test "completing a plan-generated job with no agreed price completes without crashing and skips its invoice" do
    %{user: owner, scope: scope} = owner_scope_fixture()
    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})
    property = property_fixture(scope, client)

    {:ok, {_plan, [job]}} =
      Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(scope, %{
        property_id: property.id,
        recurrence: :weekly,
        start_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
        occurrence_count: 1
      })

    refute job.agreed_price_cents

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponentTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{Job, RecurringPlan}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent

  # Hosts the component in isolation (no router route required), same
  # pattern as ClientLive.PropertyFormComponentTest.
  defmodule Host do
    use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

    @impl true
    def mount(_params, session, socket) do
      {:ok,
       assign(socket, %{
         test_pid: session["test_pid"],
         current_scope: session["scope"],
         action: session["action"],
         plan: session["plan"]
       })}
    end

    @impl true
    def render(assigns) do
      ~H"""
      <.live_component
        module={PlanFormComponent}
        id="plan-form"
        current_scope={@current_scope}
        action={@action}
        plan={@plan}
      />
      """
    end

    @impl true
    def handle_info({PlanFormComponent, _} = message, socket) do
      send(socket.assigns.test_pid, message)
      {:noreply, socket}
    end
  end

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp render_host(session) do
    session = Map.put(session, "test_pid", self())
    live_isolated(build_conn(), Host, session: session)
  end

  defp first_visit_date, do: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)
  defp visit_date(n), do: Date.add(first_visit_date(), (n - 1) * 7)

  describe "creating a recurring plan" do
    test "renders the plan form with the account's properties and cleaners" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})
      property_fixture(scope, client, %{service_address: "12 Oak Lane"})
      cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account, %{name: "Alex Morgan"})

      {:ok, _lv, html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "plan" => %RecurringPlan{}})

      assert html =~ "12 Oak Lane"
      assert html =~ "Alex Morgan"
      assert has_element?(_lv, "[data-test='save-plan-button']")
    end

    test "a conflict-free weekly series saves cleanly and materializes every job" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "plan" => %RecurringPlan{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='plan-form']",
        plan: %{
          property_id: property.id,
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          recurrence: "weekly",
          start_date: Date.to_iso8601(first_visit_date()),
          occurrence_count: 8
        }
      )
      |> render_change()

      lv
      |> element("[data-test='save-plan-button']")
      |> render_click()

      assert_receive {PlanFormComponent, {:saved, %RecurringPlan{} = plan}}
      assert Repo.aggregate(Job, :count) == 8
      refute has_element?(lv, "[data-test^='conflict-visit-']")
      assert plan.occurrence_count == 8
    end

    test "flags a conflicting later occurrence without blocking the save, and keeps showing it after" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      availability_block_fixture(scope, cleaner, %{date: visit_date(4), all_day: true})

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "plan" => %RecurringPlan{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='plan-form']",
        plan: %{
          property_id: property.id,
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          recurrence: "weekly",
          start_date: Date.to_iso8601(first_visit_date()),
          occurrence_count: 8
        }
      )
      |> render_change()

      lv
      |> element("[data-test='save-plan-button']")
      |> render_click()

      assert_receive {PlanFormComponent, {:saved, _plan}}
      assert Repo.aggregate(Job, :count) == 8

      html = render(lv)
      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='conflict-visit-4']")
      assert html =~ "Visit 4"
      refute has_element?(lv, "[data-test='conflict-visit-1']")
    end

    test "shows conflicts and override controls as a live preview before saving" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      availability_block_fixture(scope, cleaner, %{date: visit_date(4), all_day: true})
      availability_block_fixture(scope, cleaner, %{date: visit_date(7), all_day: true})

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "plan" => %RecurringPlan{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='plan-form']",
        plan: %{
          property_id: property.id,
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          recurrence: "weekly",
          start_date: Date.to_iso8601(first_visit_date())
        }
      )
      |> render_change()

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='plan-form']", plan: %{occurrence_count: 8})
      |> render_change()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='conflict-visit-4']")
      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='conflict-visit-7']")
      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='override-conflict-4']")
      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='override-conflict-7']")
      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='save-plan-button']")
      assert Repo.aggregate(Job, :count) == 0
    end

    test "overriding a conflict removes its warning" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      availability_block_fixture(scope, cleaner, %{date: visit_date(4), all_day: true})

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "plan" => %RecurringPlan{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='plan-form']",
        plan: %{
          property_id: property.id,
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          recurrence: "weekly",
          start_date: Date.to_iso8601(first_visit_date()),
          occurrence_count: 8
        }
      )
      |> render_change()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='conflict-visit-4']")

      lv
      |> element("[data-test='override-conflict-4']")
      |> render_click()

      refute has_element?(lv, "[data-test='conflict-visit-4']")
    end
  end
end

import Config

# Only in tests, remove the complexity from the password hashing algorithm
config :bcrypt_elixir, :log_rounds, 1

# Configure your database
#
# The MIX_TEST_PARTITION environment variable can be used
# to provide built-in test partitioning in CI environment.
# Run `mix help test` for more information.
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Repo,
  username: "postgres",
  password: "postgres",
  hostname: "localhost",
  database: "cleaner_crm_test#{System.get_env("MIX_TEST_PARTITION")}",
  pool: Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox,
  pool_size: System.schedulers_online() * 2

# Wallaby feature tests (test/journeys/) drive a real browser against a
# real HTTP endpoint, so the server has to actually run in test — plain
# ConnCase tests are unaffected, they never issue real HTTP requests.
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  http: [ip: {127, 0, 0, 1}, port: 4002],
  secret_key_base: "pKeS+s2UVTkO2arvvgQLttUR3McIVtITSdLygq0I9T9C5M+7mGuWBFFVOWsO/ZMR",
  server: true

# Lets the endpoint inject the Ecto sandbox metadata plug (see
# lib/cleaner_crm_web/endpoint.ex) so Wallaby's real HTTP requests share
# the test process's DB sandbox connection.
config :cleaner_crm, :sql_sandbox, true

config :wallaby,
  otp_app: :cleaner_crm,
  driver: Wallaby.Chrome,
  chromedriver: [headless: true]

# In test we don't send emails
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Mailer, adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Test

# Never reach the real Stripe API in test — see CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Test
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway,
  adapter: CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Test

# Oban runs inline in test — jobs execute synchronously in the calling
# process instead of a background queue, per the background-jobs-oban ADR.
config :cleaner_crm, Oban, testing: :inline

# Never reach the real Twilio API in test — see CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Test
config :cleaner_crm, :sms_delivery_adapter, CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Test

# Disable swoosh api client as it is only required for production adapters
config :swoosh, :api_client, false

# Print only warnings and errors during test
config :logger, level: :warning

# Initialize plugs at runtime for faster test compilation
config :phoenix, :plug_init_mode, :runtime

# Enable helpful, but potentially expensive runtime checks
config :phoenix_live_view,
  enable_expensive_runtime_checks: true

# Sort query params output of verified routes for robust url comparisons
config :phoenix,
  sort_verified_routes_query_params: true

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistComponentTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp owner_scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{user: user, scope: %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}}
  end

  # Regression for the accepted issue: completing a job with no agreed
  # price crashed invoice generation on the `invoices.amount_cents` NOT
  # NULL constraint. An unpriced recurring plan materializes visits
  # with no price (`CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1`), so
  # this drives that exact real-usage path end to end: create such a
  # plan, then complete the job it generated through the live UI.
  test "completing a plan-generated job with no agreed price completes without crashing and skips its invoice" do
    %{user: owner, scope: scope} = owner_scope_fixture()
    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})
    property = property_fixture(scope, client)

    {:ok, {_plan, [job]}} =
      Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(scope, %{
        property_id: property.id,
        recurrence: :weekly,
        start_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
        occurrence_count: 1
      })

    refute job.agreed_price_cents

    conn = log_in_user(build_conn(), owner)
    {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{job.id}")

    html =
      job_live
      |> element("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")
      |> render_click()

    assert html =~ "Complete"

    assert Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job.id).status == :completed
    assert Billing.list_invoices(scope) == []
  end
end

content.content:
Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve as
both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development workflows.

Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup blocks:
- setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
- setup: State reset between tests
- Context passing between test steps
- Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

## Usage

    mix spex                    # Run all spex files
    mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
    mix spex --help             # Show this help

## Options

    --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
    --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
    --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
    --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
    --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow
    --trace         Enable ExUnit trace mode (shows test execution details)
    --slowest N     Print timing information for the N slowest tests
    --formatter     ExUnit formatter module (default: ExUnit.CLIFormatter)
                    Can be specified multiple times
    --jsonl [PATH]  Output failures as JSONL (default: spex_failures.jsonl)
    --stale         Only run spex files that have changed or reference changed modules
    --force         Force all spex files to run (use with --stale to reset)

## Examples

    mix spex
    mix spex test/spex/user_login_spex.exs
    mix spex --pattern "**/integration_*_spex.exs"
    mix spex --verbose
    mix spex --manual           # Interactive step-by-step mode
    mix spex --speed slow       # Slower automatic execution

I've fixed the nil-price invoice crash and resolved the accepted issue. Summary:

**Plan/price plumbing** (`lib/cleaner_crm/scheduling/recurring_plan.ex`, `recurrence.ex`, `plan_form_component.ex`, plus migration `priv/repo/migrations/20260708120000_add_agreed_price_cents_to_recurring_plans.exs`): `RecurringPlan` now carries an optional `agreed_price_cents`, `Recurrence.job_attrs/1` copies it onto every materialized job, and the plan form gained a "Price ($)" input (with edit-display conversion mirroring the existing job form pattern).

**Billing** (`lib/cleaner_crm/billing.ex`, `billing/invoice.ex`): `generate_for_job/2` now returns `{:error, :no_price}` for a nil-priced job before ever touching the database, with the behavior documented in its doc. `Invoice.changeset/2` independently requires `amount_cents` after deriving it from `amount`, as a second line of defense for any other caller of `create_invoice/2`. Job completion can no longer crash on a nil price — it simply skips the invoice.

**Tests added**: `test/cleaner_crm/billing_test.exs`, `test/cleaner_crm/scheduling/recurrence_test.exs`, `test/cleaner_crm_web/live/field_live/checklist_component_test.exs` (the last one drives the exact real-world crash path end-to-end: an unpriced recurring plan's job completed through the live UI), plus a new case in `plan_form_component_test.exs` confirming a plan's price carries to all its materialized jobs.

**Verification**: `MIX_ENV=test mix compile` clean; `PORT=4002 MIX_ENV=test mix test` → 170 tests, 0 failures (includes Wallaby journeys); `mix spex` on stories 836/833/846 → 6/7/5 all green; `mix format` clean. No dev server or release rebuild was touched. The issue has been resolved in CodeMySpec and the team lead has been notified with full details.
